about.lead: I'm a web developer who enjoys building web applications and learning new things.
about.body:
I'm currently working as a Web Developer Intern at CV Access Media, gaining experience through real-world projects.

I started learning through personal projects and competitions, including LKS Web Technology and an IoT project at school. I'm always looking for new things to learn and ways to improve my skills. Currently, I'm also interested in learning more about cloud technologies.
about.currentlyIntoText: Cloud tech — Linux, Docker, AWS, CI/CD, SQL Server

intro.title: The internship
intro.text: Sixteen weeks as a web developer intern at CV Access Media — building client websites, learning servers and pipelines, and keeping a note of every lesson on the way.
intro.caption: the basics
intro.note: I kept this journal so the lessons would not fade.

outro.title: End of PKL, start of more
outro.text: The internship ended, but the notebook stayed open. These are the lessons I am carrying into the next project.
outro.caption: what I keep
outro.note: thank you to everyone who let me learn on real work.
outro.signature: see you in the next project
list: Build first, learn from what breaks
Deploy early, even when it is scary
Write it down — future you will thank you

w01.label: WEEK 01
w01.title: First day, first desk
bullets: Met the team and learned how the studio runs
Got familiar with the workplace and its tools
First task: reviewing the Access Media website
w01.learned: how a small studio plans and splits real client work
w01.challenge: everything was new — names, tools, and habits
w01.win: survived week one and shipped a first small fix
w01.note: nervous on Monday, comfortable by Friday

w02.label: WEEK 02
w02.title: Databases, replicated
bullets: Kept notes on every command that mattered
w02.learned: why production data is copied, and how
w02.challenge: one wrong config and the replica stopped silently
w02.note: config files are just picky recipes

w03.label: WEEKS 03–04
w03.title: NihonAccess & first commits
bullets: Started designing the NihonAccess Japanese course site
Made my first real commits and pull requests
Kept the layout tidy and reusable
w03.learned: version control is a habit, not a tool
w03.challenge: merging a branch without losing work
w03.win: a first page I was genuinely proud of

w04.label: WEEK 05
w04.title: Automation with GitHub Actions
bullets: Learned how YAML describes a workflow
w04.learned: how a single push can trigger a whole pipeline

w05.label: WEEK 06
w05.title: Linux, VPS & first deploy
bullets: Practiced deploying a website to a VPS
Set up SSH, domains, and folders
w05.learned: the command line does not forgive typos
w05.challenge: the first deploy broke twice before it worked
w05.win: a website live on my own server
w05.note: the first deploy was terrifying — and addictive

w06.label: WEEK 07
w06.title: Karoto takes shape
bullets: Started designing the Karoto car workshop site
Planned the structure and page flow
Reviewed the design with the team
w06.learned: design in the browser, not only in your head
w06.challenge: making a workshop site feel trustworthy

w07.label: WEEK 08
w07.title: Karoto goes live
bullets: Finished and deployed the Karoto website
Checked the site on real devices
w07.learned: shipping is a process, not a moment
w07.challenge: catching the bugs only real browsers show
w07.win: Karoto live and used by the client
w07.note: from mockup to a real URL

w08.label: WEEK 09
w08.title: WhatsApp & client data
bullets: Connected a message flow to the project
w08.challenge: matching the API to what the client needed
w08.note: APIs are just very strict conversations

w09.label: WEEKS 10–12
w09.title: Building and polishing Karoto
bullets: Fixed details reported by the client
w09.challenge: keeping several projects moving at once

w10.label: WEEK 13
w10.title: Domains & my own VPS
bullets: Explored VPS options and bought one
w10.learned: how a domain actually finds a server
w10.challenge: DNS records took longer to click than expected
w10.note: my own little machine on the internet

w11.label: WEEK 14
w11.title: Cloudflare & Nalar
bullets: Set up DNS, caching, and protection
w11.learned: what sits between a visitor and the server
w11.challenge: caching rules that cached a little too well
w11.note: the invisible layer that saves the day

w12.label: WEEK 15
w12.title: Docker & CI/CD
w12.learned: containers make “works on my machine” honest

w13.label: WEEK 16
w13.title: Portfolio & looking back
bullets: Documented the PKL process on this Journey page
w13.challenge: turning three months into something readable
w13.win: a portfolio and a journal to show for it
w13.note: the end of PKL, the start of the next thing
